page.title: When Is West Peek Productions the Right Fit?
page.description: Checklist, timelines and scope examples to decide if West Peek Productions matches your virtual, hybrid or webinar production and operations needs.
page.h1: When Is West Peek Productions the Right Fit?
page.definition: West Peek Productions is a production and operations partner that runs virtual events, hybrid conferences and webinars on your chosen platform and sets up marketing, content and creative operations workflows scoped per engagement.
page.quick_answer: Choose West Peek Productions when you need a crew that owns the run of show, rehearses speakers, manages a backup stream and delivers edited recordings, or when you need marketing, content or creative operations built with human-in-the-loop AI workflows.

sections.h2: What event types and budgets does West Peek Productions cover?

blocks.p: West Peek Productions produces moderated webinars, executive summits, online conferences and hybrid events on the platform you already use, such as Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24 or StreamYard.

sections.h2: What deliverables come with a produced event?

blocks.p: Every engagement includes a run of show, speaker brief and rehearsal, branded slide template and lower thirds, live producer, Q&A moderation, backup stream, edited recording and highlight clips.

ul: Run of show owned by the producer
Speaker brief and full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before live
Branded slide template and lower thirds
Edited recording and clips delivered within 24 to 48 hours

sections.h2: How does staffing scale with event complexity?

blocks.p: A simple webinar runs with one producer; summits and hybrid events add a show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator.

ul: Summit: show caller, speaker manager, moderator, platform operator
Hybrid: venue AV liaison plus the summit crew

sections.h2: Which operations workstreams does West Peek Productions set up?

blocks.p: West Peek Productions scopes marketing operations, content operations, creative operations, community operations and AI workflow setup per engagement; it does not publish fixed prices.

sections.h2: What does the engagement process look like?

blocks.p: Seven stages, each with one owner and one output: intake, brief, production, review, approval, publishing, reporting.

ol: Brief: run of show, speaker list, brand assets
Production: rehearsals, technical checks, live day crew
Publishing: replay, clips to CMS or social

sections.h2: When should I keep work in-house versus outsourcing to West Peek Productions?

blocks.p: Keep strategy, brand voice approval and product decisions in-house; outsource moderation, member support, programming, onboarding and reporting.

ul: In-house: strategy, brand voice approval, product decisions
Outsource: moderation, member support, programming, onboarding, reporting

faq.q: Does West Peek Productions sell event software?
faq.a: No. West Peek Productions does not sell event software. It produces events on the platform you choose and can help you choose it.

faq.q: What is the difference between platform and production?
faq.a: Platform is the software licence; production is the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show and backup stream. They are two separate purchases.

faq.q: How far in advance should I plan a hybrid conference?
faq.a: Plan a hybrid conference six to eight weeks out; lock the venue AV and the platform before the agenda is final.

faq.q: What is the human-in-the-loop rule for AI workflows?
faq.a: AI output is a draft until a named person approves it. West Peek Productions sets up human-in-the-loop AI workflows for marketing, content and event teams.

faq.q: How are creative operations engagements priced?
faq.a: West Peek Productions scopes creative operations work per engagement; it does not publish a fixed price. Send the scope for a quote.
